questions.text: What exact command grammar and wire encoding does the standard USB-UART test shell require?
questions.default: Use 8-N-1 UART at 115200 baud and map shell read/write operations to the 32-bit register map in this specification.
questions.reason: The request specifies the shell capability and baud rate but not its syntax or framing above UART characters.
questions.answer: Use 8-N-1 UART at 115200 baud and map shell read/write operations to the 32-bit register map in this specification.

questions.text: Should the test shell use a different register map or access width?
questions.default: Use aligned 32-bit registers at byte offsets 0x00 through 0x24.
questions.reason: No register offsets or bus width are specified; this map directly covers the requested operations.
questions.answer: Use aligned 32-bit registers at byte offsets 0x00 through 0x24.

questions.text: What reset brightness and control values are desired?
questions.default: Reset brightness to 255, use UART brightness source, and leave the display enabled.
questions.reason: Full brightness and visible display make the reset state immediately observable, while source-select and display-off bits default inactive.
questions.answer: Reset brightness to 0x40 (64), use the DUTY register as the brightness source (DUTY_SRC=0), and leave the display enabled (CTRL=0x2).
questions.evidence:
- {offset: 0x01, name: DUTY,    access: RW, reset: 0x40,   bits: "[7:0] PWM duty when DUTY_SRC = 0; [31:8] read 0"}
    - {offset: 0x02, name: CTRL,    access: RW, reset: 0x2,    bits: "[0] DUTY_SRC (1 = switches SW[7:0]); [1] DISPLAY_EN; [31:2] read 0"}

questions.text: How long should button debounce qualification be?
questions.default: 100000 stable cycles of the 100 MHz clock (1 ms).
questions.reason: The request requires bounce immunity but gives no interval; 1 ms is a practical responsive default.
questions.answer: 1,000,000 stable clock cycles (10 ms at 100 MHz).

questions.text: Should the button press counters have a different width or clear mechanism?
questions.default: Use three unsigned 32-bit read-only counters that reset with the CPU reset and wrap on overflow.
questions.reason: The request requires counts but does not specify width or software clearing; 32 bits supports long scripted tests without extra side effects.
questions.answer: Use three 8-bit counters in PRESSES; each wraps at 256 and the register resets to 0. A separate clear mechanism is not specified.
questions.evidence: - {offset: 0x04, name: PRESSES, access: RO, reset: 0,      bits: "[7:0] up presses, [15:8] down, [23:16] clear; each wraps at 256"}

questions.text: What exact seven-segment signal polarity and digit ordering are required?
questions.default: Use the Nexys-style active-low multiplexed display, with AN[3:0] for the counter, AN[7:6] for brightness, and AN[5:4] blank.
questions.reason: The request identifies display positions but does not specify electrical polarity or nibble ordering.
questions.answer: Use the Nexys-style active-low multiplexed display, with AN[3:0] for the counter, AN[7:6] for brightness, and AN[5:4] blank.

questions.text: Does a brightness read return the stored UART value or the effective switch-selected value?
questions.default: The brightness register returns the stored UART value, and a separate active_brightness read-only register returns the effective value.
questions.reason: This preserves access to the UART setting when switch mode is active and makes the visible active setting script-readable.
questions.answer: A read of DUTY returns its stored value; no separate active_brightness read-only register is specified.
questions.evidence: - {offset: 0x01, name: DUTY,    access: RW, reset: 0x40,   bits: "[7:0] PWM duty when DUTY_SRC = 0; [31:8] read 0"}
